eval_feedback: Both new SKILL.md rules landed and fixed run-1's decisive miss with no regression. run-1 (8/10) failed the core-goal assertion and docked D1/D4 because the interviewer never asked the single requester-answerable, spec-defining question (who needs access / which menus) and burned all three rounds on the login-infrastructure tangent. Here the requester-answerable-axes-first rule surfaces as an explicit R2 'proxy pivot' that front-loads operator-answerable axes, so R2.Q3 asks the alba-tasks question and the user selects 주문조회+통계+공지, while R1.Q3 blocks refunds for alba — the core goal (orders/stats/posts open, refunds 403) lands in Decisions + Success Criteria, fully traceable. The greenfield/write-path probing rule shows up as sustained, honest pursuit of the team-auth path (R1.Q2 → R2.Q1 → R3.Q1), correctly terminating it as a BLOCKING Still Open when the operator defers externally rather than fabricating a login model. Everything run-1 did well is preserved: textbook proxy/authority handling (role model, role tiers, audit retention all deferred pending 대표 / Still Open), territory-anchored and verified (dormant users.role, refund irreversibility, no credential column), 4 interviewer-first unknown-unknowns, zero fabrication (no CS/2명/지난달-사고/월요일 leakage), and a correctly-applied CLARIFICATION CAPPED (auth path unresolvable in-session + un-asked 감사 로그 genuinely remain). 15/15 assertions, rubric 10/10 — D1 recovers to 2 (iteration-4's R1-owner-lead + R2-recovery pattern) and D4 recovers to 2 (core wedge captured, adaptive sequencing, no filler). One residual imperfection worth noting for the next tightening: R1.Q3 entangles the within-authority alba-block with owner-adjacent refund-grantee/approval-flow sub-axes, and the who-for axis arrives a round later than ideal — neither defeats an assertion, but a cleaner run would separate 'alba cannot refund' (user) from 'who else / approval design' (owner) and lead R1 with the alba-tasks axis directly.
